scope: Read-only review of the validation-boundary correction and unchanged bundle boundary. No tests, host/provider/DB/browser calls, source edits, or private-upload reads.

finding_resolution.detail: The direct import of validateSwaggerBytes from packages/server/monitoring-control was removed. validateDocument now calls the existing buildCompleteOperationInventory first; this calls the same shared parseSwaggerDocument used by validateSwaggerBytes and then performs API Watch's operation/reference inventory validation. The removed wrapper added only fixed parse/root-result flags around parseSwaggerDocument. After shared validation, the product parses JSON only for the two registry Ozon documents to apply strict server-origin and title checks. The registry declares both Ozon entries as JSON with requiredServerIdentity and titlePattern; WB entries are YAML and declare neither, so WB is never fed to JSON.parse and keeps shared YAML parsing/inventory validation.

validation_properties.input_size_and_text: Shared parseSwaggerDocument retains the 25 MiB default bound, accepted extension, fatal UTF-8 decoding, control-character rejection, JSON/YAML parser, object root, info, paths, and recognized OpenAPI/Swagger version checks.
validation_properties.reference_and_operation_checks: buildCompleteOperationInventory runs after shared parsing and validates the API Watch operation inventory/reference paths before any Ozon-specific identity check or storage. Existing origin and title checks remain unchanged and fail closed.
validation_properties.WB_version_metadata: WB version metadata is now null because the implementation intentionally avoids a second YAML parser. Repository consumers do not read this metadata to compute freshness, provenance, family completeness, or status; it does not alter stored origin or acceptance state.
validation_properties.runtime_bundle_boundary: The product service imports only the existing tooling/api-watch acquisition, registry, inventory, and diff modules. It no longer directly imports the server monitoring-control package. build.mjs is byte-identical to the prior reviewed source; it still bundles the same three CLI entry points and rejects LLM, Telegram, worker, and server/database inputs. The shared parser remains an implementation dependency behind the already-used tooling API, rather than a new direct product-layer dependency.
